figure_alt_text.alt: A common RF tone reaches two receivers through separate fixtures at P. LO inputs enter at L; analog IF outputs at Q pass through acquisition and channelization to O, where channel 2 is compared with channel 1.

A shared source splits through endpoint delays, or through delayed local reference responses, with additive output noise on each path. Varying shared-LO branch noise moves the selected-band phase standard deviation through the 1.5-degree criterion and reverses the conditional preference.

Known RF comb tones pass through two fixtures and receivers with fixed 990 MHz LO inputs. Analog IF outputs are acquired at 32 Msample/s, then separated into 100 ksample/s complex streams per tone; the 1000.5 MHz tone is held out.

A 2 ns phase slope through three training frequencies predicts a withheld fourth tone. Its mean intercept differs from the 1 GHz intercept. Correct carrier subtraction leaves a sloping residual; subtracting the mean phase also leaves a carrier bias.

The calibration snapshot is centered before its coefficient is applied. Wanted data is gated through settling, collection and after-end processing. The previous coefficient ages until replacement; bounded drift remains below 0.5 degree for the two illustrative cases, separately from snapshot uncertainty.

A held correction changes at update times while a frozen correction stays constant. Under independent errors and randomized grid origin, covariance falls linearly to zero at one update period and the two-sided PSD has sinc-squared sidelobes away from DC.

A sequence from reset through acquisition, resolved branch and applicable calibration, held-out model checking and independent validity evidence reaches valid use. Failure or invalidation gates data and returns to acquisition.

The source and fixtures feed a receiver pair ending at Q1 and Q2. Main and separate acquisition chains observe the same IF phase through different readout errors. Subtracting readings cancels their shared receiver phase; controlled fixture and acquisition swaps reverse different terms.

Five bounded scalar intervals lie below, touch, overlap or lie above an upper limit. Acceptance permits the upper endpoint at the limit; rejection requires the lower endpoint strictly above it, leaving overlap and lower-endpoint equality inconclusive.
A common RF tone feeds two receivers through fixtures; analog IF and acquired complex output planes are distinguished before comparing channel 2 with channel 1.

Incoming phase and detector noise drive an oscillator correction through negative feedback. The estimate contains positive filtered noise; the true residual contains its negative, while detector output adds the original noise.

The estimate retains slow input phase while the residual suppresses it. Increasing corner frequency lowers rate bias but admits more detector noise, leaving a bounded range meeting the illustrative residual RMS criterion.

Below unit normalized rate there are stable and unstable phase equilibria; at equality attraction is only one-sided and above it phase slips. Holdover reaches the 0.1 rad bound at 0.127324 seconds, and marginal latency decreases as one over loop corner.
Delay uncertainty increases when shared-source draws decorrelate or their path sensitivities differ; common cancellation meets the target only under closely matched observation conditions.

A flat first-order tangent predicts zero uncertainty while the exact and second-order calculations give nonzero output scatter and preserve the symmetry between positive and negative phase deviations.
Direct subtraction loses accuracy at short observation ratios, while the local series remains close to a high-precision reference.
A negative phase-frequency slope gives 5 ns total delay; halving the observation span doubles delay standard deviation and crosses the illustrative 2 ns target.
Two different unwrapped slopes have identical wrapped samples at integer MHz offsets, while conditional off-grid predictions distinguish the branches.
A shared phase source branches with sensitivities one and two into two channels, while independent local errors enter their own channels.

A full covariance ellipse and rank-one line share equal radian axes; a marked support point maps to the channel-difference projection, whose half-width is the square root of its quadratic-form variance.
Two nearly parallel response vectors become indistinguishable as sensitivity separation vanishes; inverse estimate RMS grows as one over the separation.
A complex filter followed by angle extraction differs from extracting phase first; an AM-only input yields a nonzero output angle only in the first chain.
A positive one-second box average and two oppositely signed one-second boxes show constant rejection by differencing.
Box averaging has sidelobes, increments reject DC and their product weights separated phase averages.
Phase averaging improves with time while expected coherent power falls; squared mean amplitude differs from both, and equal-variance increment laws give distinct signed coherence.
Stationary increment variance saturates at two radian squared, random-walk increment variance grows with lag and only the stationary model has the displayed absolute phase PSD.
One source reaches two delayed endpoints; exact differential gain oscillates from zero to four while the small-offset approximation eventually diverges.
Negative correlation reduces mean scatter but plus and minus correlations produce identical variance-estimator uncertainty.
Conditional Gaussian phase densities form a wider mixture; independent record means fluctuate while each random-constant record keeps its offset.
Independent noise decreases as one over square root N, record-constant noise stays fixed and mixed noise approaches 0.016 rad.
Four discrete points, circular Gaussian contours and two diagonal supports all have zero pseudo-covariance but different distributions.
Two nearly overlapping left-pointing unit vectors have a left-pointing vector mean although the arithmetic angle mean is zero.
Signal plus additive noise gives an atan2 phase; for zero parallel noise, arctangent approaches a finite angle while the linear prediction grows.
Two RF paths feed mixers with separate LO endpoints, then real IF outputs Q and common-reference complex extraction O.
Two equal-magnitude phasor pairs before and after common reference rotation retain a positive 40 degree separation.
Lower and upper LO paths give signed plus and minus 10 MHz difference tones and reports of 40 and minus 26 degrees.
Phase can advance two degrees or retreat 358 degrees between the same observations; positive waveform delay moves a sinusoid right.
Phase traces stop on either side of an amplitude-invalid interval, with no interpolating connection.
